simple.meaning: נָתַח (nâthach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to dismember.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Exodus, Leviticus, Judges, 1 Samuel, 1 Kings, beginning at Exodus 29:17. Its contexts include offering, altar, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָתַח (H5408).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָתַח (nâthach) / H5408 is traced through Exodus 29:17, Leviticus 1:6, Leviticus 1:12, Leviticus 8:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: cut (in pieces), divide, hew in pieces.
definitions.full: H5408. nathach [ נָתַח verb only Pi`el cut up, cut in pieces, divide by joints (Dr 1811, 7 ; Late Hebrew id. , Pi`el; rare); — Pi`el Perfect נִתַּח Lev 8:20 , וְנִתַּח consecutive 1:6 , 12 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיְנַתַּח 1Kin 18:33 , suffix וַיְנַתְּחֵ֫הוּ 1Sam 11:7 , וַיְנַתְּחֶ֫הָ Judg 19:29 , etc.; — cut up, in pieces , with accusative of animals 1Sam 11:7 , of woman Judg 20:6 (all these to be sent about as token for assembling warriors; on significance of the practice compare RS Sem i. 383; 2nd ed. 402 ); elsewhere usually + לִנְתָחִים , cut up into pieces , of woman 19:29 ; of sacrificial animals 1Kin 18:23 , 33 (accusative only), Exod 29:17 ; Lev 1:6 , 12 ; 8:20 (all P).

occurrences.englishText: You shall cut the ram into its pieces, and wash its innards, and its legs, and put them with its pieces, and with its head.
He shall skin the burnt offering, and cut it into pieces.
He shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat. The priest shall lay them in order on the wood that is on the fire which is on the altar,
He cut the ram into its pieces; and Moses burned the head, and the pieces, and the fat.
When he had come into his house, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel.
I took my concubine and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the country of the inheritance of Israel; for they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel.

He took a yoke of oxen, and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Whoever doesn’t come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.” The dread of Yahweh fell on the people, and they came out as one man.

Let them therefore give us two bulls; and let them choose one bull for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire under; and I will dress the other bull, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire under it.
He put the wood in order, and cut the bull in pieces, and laid it on the wood. He said, “Fill four jars with water, and pour it on the burnt offering, and on the wood.”
